customConcept.name: POPS 66 soda ranch
customConcept.blurb: A 66-foot soda bottle, a glass wall of more than 700 sodas, a diner, a gift shop and gas pumps under a hundred-foot cantilevered canopy, out on Route 66.

state.circumstances: You own POPS, the Route 66 soda ranch in Arcadia: a diner, a wall of 700 sodas, a gift shop, gas pumps and a 66-foot bottle that lights up every night.

features.name: The 66-foot soda bottle
features.pitch: Four tons of steel and more than 4,000 LEDs, lit up in a light show every night. Visible for miles down Route 66.

features.name: The soda wall
features.pitch: Glass shelves of more than 700 sodas arranged by colour, most of them for sale.

features.name: Fuel canopy and pumps
features.pitch: Gas pumps under the hundred-foot cantilevered canopy.

features.name: Gift shop
features.pitch: T-shirts, hoodies, hats and Route 66 souvenirs.

setting.name: Historic Route 66, Arcadia
setting.desc: On old Route 66 in Arcadia, a small town just east of Edmond and the Oklahoma City metro, down the road from the Round Barn. Road-trippers from all over the world in summer, OKC families on weekends, and a quiet highway in January.

ev.text: A tornado warning cleared the diner and shut the pumps for an evening. Everyone waited it out in the cooler.
A convoy of European Route 66 tour groups came through on their way west, and cleared a whole shelf of the soda wall.
A classic car club from Tulsa rolled in: forty cars parked under the canopy and on everybody's social feeds.

desk.title: A bottler wants the wall
desk.text: A craft soda brand wants to pay for its own section of the soda wall for a year, front and centre.

choices.label: Sell them the shelf
choices.blurb: Money now, and one less shelf of oddities.

ev.text: A few of the LEDs on the bottle burned out and the light show ran patchy for a week.

kit.model: Existing exhaust fan & duct, no makeup air
A couple of old ABC extinguishers
Commercial bentwood chairs and laminate-topped tables
Rooftop units for the diner and the soda hall
A standard set: hotel pans, sheet pans, knives and scales
Ice cream dipping cabinet for the hand-dipped cones and shakes

mods.label: Property tax, insurance and the 66-foot bottle's lights

world.notes: This is POPS 66 in Arcadia, Oklahoma, on historic Route 66: opened in 2007, designed by Elliott + Associates Architects, with a 66-foot, four-ton steel soda bottle lit by more than 4,000 LEDs, a 100-foot cantilevered canopy over the gas pumps, and glass walls lined with more than 700 sodas sorted by colour. The diner serves Angus burgers, weekend breakfast and hand-dipped shakes and floats at the prices on its current menu; the store is open 6am to 10pm and the diner 10:30am to 9pm, with breakfast from 7am on weekends. Soda, fuel and merchandise sales are modelled as side revenue. The seat count, sales and property value are estimates, and staff names are invented; the player is not the real owners. It's a dry, family place: no alcohol.
